To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ecology and palaoecology have historically progressed as two separate disciplines, that this separation has been caused by a combination of factors including the past-present dissociative human mind, the diversity of fields from which palaeoecolgoists come, the contrasting nature of evidence and methods, and misunderstandings caused by use of the prefix palao-.
ecology and palaoeocology have progressed historically well separated disciplines and that this unfortunate disjunction is analysed here from a theoretical perspective.

1) the biosphere is a time continuum through the past, present and the future, 2) ecology and palaeontology are only different ways of approaching the study of the biosphere, 3) ecology in a broad sense includes inferences about past, present and projected future, 4) palaeoecological studies are a means by which ecological studies are conducted on the past using proxies, 5) other disciplines beginning with the suffix palaeo- are not necessarily ecological
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ecology of the past, and we are ecologists.
the past, but our objective is to understand the biosphere in the present, and the future.
the past and present of the biosphere and its evolution, and the future of the human species and its environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ecology is the study of the interactions between organisms and their environment, and palaeo- ecology is the study on the past of those interactions.

palaeoecological data and methods are of interest for ecological studies; palaeoecologically oriented ecologists are palaeoecoscientists; and, conversely, palaeoecologially oriented palaeoscientists are palaeo-ecologists.
palaeo-ecology is ecology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ecology is the study of the biosphere and palaeo-ecology is the study of past biospheres.
ecology and palaoecology are not separate fields but complementary approaches that together provide a more complete view of the biosphere and the processes that drive its functioning and evolution.
ecology and palaoecology are not two disciplines but one, which has two approaches to the same objective: understanding the biosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ecology and palaoecology are two approaches, one objective.
the future of palaeo-ecology depends on its integration into mainstream ecology, and that the future of ecology depends on the development of palaeo-eocology.
ecology and palaoeocology are two sides of the same coin, and that the two disciplines can be integrated into one, with ecology as its common denominator.
